subject: In isolated mitral regurgitation, total left ventricular stroke volume
object: both forward flow into the aorta and backward flow through the mitral valve. In mitral regurgitation, reduced left ventricular afterload keeps ejection fraction normal or above normal until advanced disease. Measures such as ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain therefore overestimate left ventricular contractility.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: Hence, in patients with isolated MR, the LV total stroke volume (LVTSV) equals the aortic forward stroke volume (anterograde flow) plus the mitral RegVol (retrograde flow). A particular problem of MR is that LV afterload is reduced, so the LVEF remains normal or supranormal until the disease reaches an advanced stage. Therefore, parameters such as LVEF or global longitudinal strain over-estimate LV contractility ().

subject: Assessment of the mitral valve leaflets, annulus and subvalvular apparatus
object: before measurements. Carpentier's classification of leaflet motion is used to identify the mechanisms of loss of leaflet coaptation and helps distinguish primary disease due to organic leaflet abnormalities from secondary disease due to left ventricular dysfunction and/or high left atrial pressure. Prolapse, perforation, a flail leaflet or papillary muscle rupture makes primary regurgitation relatively easy to identify.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: Before to compute any measurement, the full assessment of all components of the MV apparatus (leaflets, annulus, sub-valvular apparatus) is critical. The mechanism(s) underpinning mitral loss of coaptation are evaluated according to Carpentier's classification of leaflet motion. This approach allows to distinguish patients with primary MR (due to organic leaflet abnormalities) to those with secondary MR (due to LV dysfunction and/or high LA pressure) (). It is relatively easy to classify MR as primary in in the presence of obvious valve abnormalities such as prolapse, perforation, flail, or papillary muscle rupture.

subject: Secondary or functional mitral regurgitation
object: functional abnormalities of the left heart chambers. An imbalance between leaflet closing forces and tethering leads to poor or incomplete leaflet coaptation. Its two main forms are atrial and ventricular.
source: Article: Iliakis P, Dimitriadis K, Pyrpyris N et al. Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation: From Diagnosis to Current Interventional Therapies. Journal of Clinical Medicine 2024
source_quote: Functional or secondary mitral regurgitation (FMR) is defined as mitral regurgitation (MR) and is mainly attributed to functional abnormalities of left heart chambers . The key pathophysiology basis of secondary MR is a disturbance in the balance between the closure forces and the tethering of mitral leaflets, which leads to poor or incomplete coaptation . The two main morphological forms of FMR are atrial and ventricular FMR.

subject: In advanced mitral regurgitation, or after it worsens acutely, for example after sudden chordal rupture, symptoms

source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: Consequences of MR on cardiac remodeling In more advanced stage of the disease (or in case of acute worsening, for example due to sudden chordae rupture), symptoms occur, alongside with LV systolic dysfunction and/or pulmonary hypertension ().

subject: In ventricular functional mitral regurgitation, regional or global left ventricular remodelling and dysfunction
object: apical tethering of the mitral leaflets. This form is associated with many ischaemic and non-ischaemic diseases affecting left ventricular myocytes.
source: Article: Iliakis P, Dimitriadis K, Pyrpyris N et al. Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation: From Diagnosis to Current Interventional Therapies. Journal of Clinical Medicine 2024
source_quote: In left ventricular functional MR (VFMR), the left ventricle (LV) undergoes regional or global remodeling and dysfunction, resulting in apical tethering of the mitral leaflets. It has been associated with numerous diseases (ischemic or not) affecting left ventricular myocytes .

subject: Atrial functional mitral regurgitation, the less common form,
object: annular enlargement associated with marked left atrial dilatation while left ventricular size and function are preserved.
source: Article: Iliakis P, Dimitriadis K, Pyrpyris N et al. Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation: From Diagnosis to Current Interventional Therapies. Journal of Clinical Medicine 2024
source_quote: On the other hand, atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR) refers to the less common condition, in which MR, caused by annular enlargement, is associated with remarkable dilatation of the left atrium (LA) while both LV size and function are preserved .

subject: Atrial fibrillation mainly impairs atrial contraction and removes the atrial kick, so annular motion
object: driven by the ventricle. Loss of the atrial contribution to contraction during diastole has been proposed as a cause of developing and worsening atrial functional mitral regurgitation because it promotes poor and delayed leaflet coaptation. Loss of the late-diastolic reduction in annular size leaves a larger annulus, increases the mismatch between annulus and leaflets and results in regurgitation.
source: Article: Iliakis P, Dimitriadis K, Pyrpyris N et al. Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation: From Diagnosis to Current Interventional Therapies. Journal of Clinical Medicine 2024
source_quote: AF predominantly affects the capability of the atrium to contract, resulting in a loss of the “atrial kick” and therefore leading to ventricular-based annular mechanics. The loss of the atrial contractive contribution during diastole has been postulated as one of the culprits of AFMR pathogenesis and progression, promoting leaflet malcoaptation and delayed coaptation. In particular, the loss of annular size reduction during end-diastole results in a larger annular area, which enhances the annulus-leaflet imbalance, thus resulting in blood volume regurgitation.

subject: Chronic primary mitral regurgitation
object: left atrial volume overload and later pressure overload. Left ventricular stroke volume must compensate for the regurgitant volume to maintain forward stroke volume. This gradually dilates the left ventricle through the Frank-Starling mechanism.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: Chronic primary MR causes direct volume overload on the LA and in later stages pressure overload. In addition, the left ventricular stroke volume (LVSV) must compensate for the mitral RegVol to maintain LV forward stroke volume. This will progressively lead to LV dilatation according to the Frank-Starling law.

subject: A triangular continuous-wave Doppler signal from a mitral regurgitant jet with an early peak and low velocity
object: severe regurgitation. It can occur in acute severe regurgitation when excess volume rapidly overwhelms left atrial compliance, raising left atrial pressure and reducing the pressure driving flow from the left ventricle to the left atrium.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: A triangular-shaped CWD MR signal with early peaking and low velocity supports severe MR (). It can be observed notably in acute severe MR when LA compliance is quickly overwhelmed by excess volume load, resulting in high LA pressure and decreased LV-LA driving pressure.

subject: Initial assessment of mitral regurgitation
object: a full medical and medication history, complete physical examination with cardiac auscultation and an ECG. Recognising valve-related symptoms such as breathlessness takes experience, especially in older people who are likely to limit daily activities without reporting complaints at assessment.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: The evaluation of a patient with MR begins with a full report of her/his past medical history, previous medication regimens and a complete physical examination with heart auscultation and electrocardiography (ECG). Search for potential valve-related symptoms such as dyspnea requires experience, especially in older patients who are likely to limit themselves in daily activities without reporting any complaint at the time of evaluation.

subject: Transthoracic echocardiography
relation: is the main imaging test for
object: assessing the mechanism, cause, severity and likelihood of repair in mitral regurgitation.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the mainstay imaging modality for assessing the mechanism, etiology, severity, and repair probability of MR ().

subject: The echocardiographic parameters for grading mitral regurgitation
object: qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative. Qualitative red flags are highly specific for severe regurgitation but lack sensitivity. Semi-quantitative measures indicate mild or severe disease but have a large inconclusive intermediate range. Quantitative measures estimate effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume and regurgitant fraction.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: The echocardiographic parameters used to grade MR are classically divided into three main categories: qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative. The qualitative approach consists in the search for “red flags”, that is echocardiographic signs highly specific of severe MR but lacking sensitivity. The semi-quantitative echocardiographic parameters are measurements indicative of MR grade (mild or severe) but including a large intermediate range of values where no conclusion on MR severity can be made. Finally, the quantitative approach intends to estimate the key components of MR which are the mitral effective regurgitant orifice area [EROA], regurgitant volume [RegVol] and regurgitant fraction [RegFrac].

subject: When transthoracic echocardiography gives suboptimal or inconclusive quantification of mitral regurgitation, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and/or transoesophageal echocardiography
object: complementary information. Transoesophageal echocardiography helps grade severity and offers its greatest advantage over the other two tests in detailed assessment of the lesions and mechanisms, especially when planning mitral valve surgery.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: When TTE is suboptimal or inconclusive for MR quantification, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and/or transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) provide complementary information. Indeed, TEE helps in grading MR severity, although its strongest advantage over TTE or CMR is to offer a comprehensive assessment of the anatomical lesions and mechanism(s) of MR, especially when planning MV surgery ().

subject: Exercise transthoracic echocardiography for mitral regurgitation
object: clinical and haemodynamic tolerance of the regurgitation. Quantifying severity is a separate assessment.
source: Article: Altes A, Vermes E, Levy F et al. Quantification of primary mitral regurgitation by echocardiography: A practical appraisal. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2023
source_quote: The role of exercise TTE is to ascertain key information on the clinical and hemodynamic tolerance of MR rather than to help in quantifying MR severity ().
